# Pitloom's catalogued messages: Network

See also: `messages.md` (the index of every code), `../SKILL.md` (which holds
the rule: explain and relay, never run the fix).

Trust a code only when the line is one of the lines below, a value in place of
each `<name>`, after at most one prefix: the index lists the prefixes and

### `download-network-failed`

- **Level**: ERROR, WARNING. As an ERROR, the command stops for that input and
  writes nothing for it (exit 1).
- **Means**: A request to a remote source failed. PyPI, a Hugging Face file: an
  HTTP status other than 404 (a 401 or 403 for a private or gated repository
  read without access), a refused or reset connection, a name that did not
  resolve, or an answer cut short. A Croissant document a library caller names
  by URL (read_croissant): the same, any HTTP error status, a 404 included. The
  Hugging Face Hub API (model_info(), dataset_info()): any HTTP error status, a
  404 for a repository that does not exist or is private included, or a
  connection that failed. Git: git could not reach the repository (a name that
  did not resolve, a refused, reset or timed-out connection, a TLS failure, an
  HTTP 5xx answer); a git failure with any other cause is
  git-repository-unusable.
- **SBOM effect**: not-written: no SBOM is written for the input.
- **Pitloom did**: Wrote no SBOM (the error: pypi.download-failed,
  git.clone-failed; read_croissant raises ValueError carrying the code); for a
  Hugging Face file, left that file out and read the rest; for a Hub API
  request, recorded none of what it states, as the line's outcome names, and
  read the rest (the warning).
- **Tell the user**: the request failed, with the reason the line gives. They
  check the network and run again; for a private or gated Hugging Face
  repository (HTTP 401 or 403) they sign in with an account that has access
  (HF_TOKEN, or 'hf auth login'). Do not retry in a loop or sign in for them;
  ask first, and with nobody to ask, report it only.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  ERROR: URL=<url>: <failure>; not read [download-network-failed]
  ERROR: git <command> failed: <error>; nothing fetched [download-network-failed]
  WARNING: URL=<url>: <failure>; <outcome> [download-network-failed]
  ```

### `download-timeout`

- **Level**: ERROR, WARNING. As an ERROR, the command stops for that input and
  writes nothing for it (exit 1).
- **Means**: A request to PyPI, to the host that serves a file (a Croissant
  document a library caller names by URL included) or to the Hugging Face Hub (a
  file, or the API's model_info() or dataset_info()), or the git calls that
  fetch a repository, did not finish within the time Pitloom allows.
- **SBOM effect**: not-written: no SBOM is written for the input.
- **Pitloom did**: Stopped the request and wrote no SBOM (the error:
  pypi.download-timeout, git.timeout; read_croissant raises ValueError carrying
  the code); for a Hugging Face file, left that file out and read the rest; for
  a Hub API request, recorded none of what it states, as the line's outcome
  names, and read the rest (the warning).
- **Tell the user**: the request timed out. They check the network and run
  again, or fetch the file or repository themselves and run Pitloom on the local
  copy. Do not retry in a loop; ask first, and with nobody to ask, report it
  only.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  ERROR: URL=<url>: no complete answer within <seconds> seconds; not read [download-timeout]
  ERROR: git <command> did not finish within <seconds> seconds; stopped [download-timeout]
  WARNING: URL=<url>: no complete answer within <seconds> seconds; <outcome> [download-timeout]
  ```

### `hub-response-invalid`

- **Level**: WARNING.
- **Means**: The Hugging Face Hub answered model_info() or dataset_info() with
  something huggingface_hub or Pitloom could not read: not JSON, or JSON without
  the shape the API gives.
- **SBOM effect**: thinner: the SBOM says less than reading the input would.
- **Pitloom did**: Recorded none of what the request states, as the line's
  outcome names, and read the rest.
- **Tell the user**: the Hub's answer was not usable, as the line says. They may
  run again later; with HF_ENDPOINT set, the Hub it names may not speak the
  Hugging Face API. Do not change HF_ENDPOINT for them; ask first, and with
  nobody to ask, report it only.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  WARNING: URL=<url>: the Hub's answer could not be read (<failure>); <outcome> [hub-response-invalid]
  ```

### `hub-revision-unpinned`

- **Level**: WARNING.
- **Means**: model_info() stated no revision (commit hash) of a Hugging Face
  model: the request failed, or the Hub (a mirror, a private Hub) sent none. Its
  files (config.json, the model card, a licence file) are read at the default
  branch as it is at the time of the run, which can change between runs.
- **SBOM effect**: weaker: what the SBOM says is less sure.
- **Pitloom did**: Read the model's files at the default branch (said once per
  read of a model, however many files); the SBOM records no version of the
  model.
- **Tell the user**: the files were read without a revision, so a later run can
  read other files. Nothing they pass to Pitloom pins it; for a repeatable
  result they download the repository at a commit and run Pitloom on the local
  copy. Do not download it for them; ask first, and with nobody to ask, report
  it only.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  WARNING: URL=<url>: the Hub stated no revision; files are read at the default branch as it is now [hub-revision-unpinned]
  ```

### `offline-unusable`

- **Level**: ERROR, WARNING. As an ERROR, the command stops for that input and
  writes nothing for it (exit 1).
- **Means**: Offline mode is on and the target must be fetched: a Git URL, a
  PyPI URL or a Hugging Face repository. Offline mode is --offline, the offline
  key of --config, or offline=True; for a file of a Hugging Face repository, or
  the Hub API's model_info() and dataset_info(), also huggingface_hub's own
  HF_HUB_OFFLINE.
- **SBOM effect**: not-written: no SBOM is written for the input.
- **Pitloom did**: Fetched nothing and wrote no SBOM (the error: git.offline,
  pypi.offline, huggingface.offline); for a Hugging Face file or Hub API request
  under HF_HUB_OFFLINE, left it out, as the line's outcome names, and read the
  rest (the warning).
- **Tell the user**: the target must be fetched and offline mode forbids it.
  They run again without offline mode (no --offline, offline = false in the
  config, HF_HUB_OFFLINE unset), or fetch the repository or file themselves and
  run Pitloom on the local copy. Do not turn offline mode off for them; ask
  first, and with nobody to ask, report it only.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  ERROR: URL=<url>: network access is forbidden (offline mode); nothing fetched [offline-unusable]
  WARNING: URL=<url>: network access is forbidden (offline mode); <outcome> [offline-unusable]
  ```

### `query-no-effect`

- **Level**: INFO.
- **Means**: The PyPI or Git URL given holds a query or a fragment (a tab of the
  page) that names no project, release, branch, tag or commit; or a Git page
  URL's version query names none of them.
- **SBOM effect**: none: the SBOM states what the input holds.
- **Pitloom did**: Read the URL without them; for a Git URL whose version names
  nothing, read the default branch.
- **Nothing to do**: nothing to do: the project and release, or the repository
  and version, are read from the rest of the URL.
- **Printed after**: `Git source: <text>` (a Git URL fetch), on its INFO lines;
  the prefix is not part of the line.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  INFO: URL=<url>: the query and fragment have no effect; cut [query-no-effect]
  INFO: URL=<url>: the version names no branch, tag or commit; the default branch is read [query-no-effect]
  ```

### `url-moved`

- **Level**: INFO.
- **Means**: PyPI, or the host serving a file, redirected a request to another
  URL on a host Pitloom reads PyPI from (a renamed project, a normalised name);
  or a Git URL, asked before git is run, redirects to another https URL of a
  repository (a renamed or moved repository).
- **SBOM effect**: none: the SBOM states what the input holds.
- **Pitloom did**: Checked the target and followed it (for a Git URL, git is run
  on the target).
- **Nothing to do**: nothing to do: the line names where the answer came from.
- **Printed after**: `Git source: <text>` (a Git URL fetch), on its INFO lines;
  the prefix is not part of the line.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  INFO: URL=<url>: redirects to <target>; followed [url-moved]
  ```

### `url-moved/hf-endpoint`

- **Level**: INFO.
- **Means**: huggingface_hub's HF_ENDPOINT names a Hub other than
  https://huggingface.co (a mirror, a private Hub).
- **SBOM effect**: none: the SBOM states what the input holds.
- **Pitloom did**: Fetched the Hugging Face files from it, the token sent to it
  only.
- **Nothing to do**: nothing to do: the line names where the files came from.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  INFO: URL=<url>: the Hub HF_ENDPOINT names; Hugging Face files are fetched from it [url-moved/hf-endpoint]
  ```

### `url-unsafe`

- **Level**: ERROR, WARNING. As an ERROR, the command stops for that input and
  writes nothing for it (exit 1).
- **Means**: Pitloom would have to send a request somewhere it does not: a
  redirect to a URL that is not https or not on a host it reads PyPI or a
  Hugging Face file from, a Git URL's redirect to a URL that is not https or not
  a repository's, more redirects than it follows, or a file whose download URL
  PyPI gives on another host.
- **SBOM effect**: not-written: no SBOM is written for the input.
- **Pitloom did**: Did not follow the redirect or fetch the file, and wrote no
  SBOM (the error: git.too-many-redirects for a Git URL); for a Hugging Face
  file, left that file out and read the rest (the warning); for a Git URL's
  redirect, ran git on the URL as given, which follows no redirect (the
  warning).
- **Tell the user**: which URL was not followed and why, as the line says. A
  mirror or proxy that redirects is not supported; they may download the file
  themselves and run Pitloom on it. Do not fetch the target for them; ask first,
  and with nobody to ask, report it only.
- **Printed after**: `Git source: <text>` (a Git URL fetch), on its WARNING
  lines; the prefix is not part of the line.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  ERROR: URL=<url>: redirects to <target>; not followed (<why>) [url-unsafe]
  ERROR: URL=<url>: more than <number> redirects; not followed [url-unsafe]
  ERROR: FILE=<file>: download URL <target> is not on <hosts>; not fetched [url-unsafe]
  WARNING: URL=<url>: redirects to <target>; not followed (<why>); <outcome> [url-unsafe]
  WARNING: URL=<url>: more than <number> redirects; <outcome> [url-unsafe]
  ```

### `url-unsafe/hf-endpoint`

- **Level**: WARNING.
- **Means**: huggingface_hub's HF_ENDPOINT names a Hub that is not an https URL,
  or one holding user information, a query or a fragment. The Hugging Face token
  must not be sent over plain http.
- **SBOM effect**: thinner: the SBOM says less than reading the input would.
- **Pitloom did**: Sent no request to the Hub (huggingface_hub would send the
  token to the same endpoint): no file of the Hugging Face repository
  (config.json, the card, a licence file), no model_info() or dataset_info().
  The model keeps its id and Hub URL only; the SBOM lacks everything else the
  Hub states.
- **Tell the user**: HF_ENDPOINT is not used, and why, as the line says. They
  set it to an https URL without credentials, or unset it for
  https://huggingface.co, and run again. Do not change it for them; ask first,
  and with nobody to ask, report it only.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  WARNING: URL=<url>: HF_ENDPOINT not used (<why>); nothing asked of the Hub [url-unsafe/hf-endpoint]
  ```

### `url-unsafe/host-spelling`

- **Level**: ERROR. As an ERROR, the command stops for that input and writes
  nothing for it (exit 1).
- **Means**: A Git URL's host holds a non-ASCII character (a full-width or
  ideographic dot, a full-width letter, an international name not in its xn--
  form) or a percent-encoding. git (through curl) maps it to another host than
  the URL's text names, past every check that reads that text (a PyPI host is
  never cloned). Or it holds a character no host name holds (=, !, ;, white
  space, a leading - or .), the shape of an option or a setting smuggled into
  git's command line, or is a name in brackets ([v1.x]), which would lose them
  and name a DNS host. An IPv6 zone id ([fe80::1%25eth0]) is refused too.
- **SBOM effect**: not-written: no SBOM is written for the input.
- **Pitloom did**: Started no git process, fetched nothing and wrote no SBOM
  (git.url-invalid).
- **Tell the user**: the host must be written as it is resolved. They write it
  in ASCII, an international domain name in its xn-- (punycode) form, and run
  again. Do not rewrite the URL for them; ask first, and with nobody to ask,
  report it only.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  ERROR: URL=<url>: the host is not plain ASCII, is percent-encoded or holds a character no host name holds (=, !, white space, a leading -), which git would resolve to a host the URL does not spell or read as an option; write it in ASCII (an international name in its xn-- form); nothing fetched [url-unsafe/host-spelling]
  ```
